title: Danau Puchong: two low-density towers on the IOI Puchong lake.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #403 | DANAU PUCHONG, PUSAT BANDAR PUCHONG
excerpt: YTL Land's 428-unit lakeside project between two LRT stations off the LDP, priced from about RM550 per sq ft. Sean likes the location, the design and the density, but not the uncertainty over the reclaimed land in front, the nearby competition or the tricky approach.
takeaways: Two towers of 214 units each, 10 units per floor served by four lifts, with a private driveway off the LDP side.
Every unit shares a 4.4 m-wide living and dining grid that frames the lake view.
One-bedroom units from about RM332,000; the 999 sq ft three-bedroom Type C Sean viewed comes to roughly RM540,000.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Danau Puchong is two towers with 428 units in total, sharing the lake beside IOI Mall Puchong. Residents reach it along a private road with the lake on one side, pass a guardhouse and a covered drop-off, and drive straight into the elevated car park, which uses split-level ramps, so it's worth checking where your bay is. The facilities deck between the car park and the towers puts an infinity pool and the gym facing the lake, with a wading pool, multipurpose hall, hammock garden, barbecue terraces and a separate children's play area. Sky gardens step the upper floors, so some floors have fewer units.

A standard floor has 10 units on a double-loaded corridor served by four lifts, with no fire doors between the lift lobby and corridor. Each unit is reached through a small foyer set between voids, which adds distance and privacy from neighbours and isn't counted in the built-up area. Sean viewed the 999 sq ft Type C, a three-bedroom unit with a linear kitchen, a 1.53 by 2.13 m yard, a 4.4 m-wide living and dining area with a 2.7 m ceiling, a 3.53 m balcony, two similar secondary bedrooms and a 3.3 by 4.5 m master bedroom. Almost no space is lost to corridors. The show unit had only air-conditioning piping, so buyers should confirm what comes with the keys.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The site sits off the LDP, Puchong's main road, between the IOI Puchong Jaya and Pusat Bandar Puchong LRT stations, with IOI Mall Puchong on one side and a Lotus's hypermarket on the other. Shop lots line the highway, and Puchong Jaya, Puchong Utama and Bandar Puteri are nearby. The quiet road into the project is shared with the developer's gated Lake Edge, launched in 2004, where a new Chinese primary school has just opened. Reclamation on the land in front is a separate developer's future project, which will have its own access from the LDP.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: One-bedroom units start from about RM332,000, and pricing works out to roughly RM550 per sq ft, so the Type C unit Sean viewed is around RM540,000 depending on floor and orientation. Sean finds that attractive for the density, location and convenience, and notes that many early buyers are Lake Edge owners buying for their children.

standout.title: A 4.4 m grid for every unit
standout.body: All units, down to the one-bedrooms, share the same 4.4 m width for the living and dining area. Against a ceiling of about 2.7 m, that proportion frames the lake like a portrait, and the generous width is something Sean usually sees only in much larger homes. The catch, he jokes, is that your TV and furniture need to grow to match.

pros: The location: on Puchong's main road between three commercial hubs, two malls and two LRT stations, yet tucked away by the lake on a quiet, private road shared with Lake Edge.

The developer's design language and track record: a private entrance that works as a prelude home, straight-in car park access, a lake-facing pool, a seamless lift lobby, foyers set between voids, sky gardens and a very efficient layout with no lost storage or yard.
The density: only 428 units, 10 per floor with four lifts, surrounded by mature developments and the lake, with nothing else around right now.
cons: The reclaimed land in front: no plans have been submitted yet, and if another tower goes up next to it, Tower B could be affected.
Competition: several similar lakeside projects are launching on the same street, so buyers need to compare design, track record, price and rent carefully.

The micro-location: the approach from the LDP is easy to get wrong the first time, the shop lots at the entrance are dated, there are pylons nearby, and Puchong has traffic jams and last year's floods near IOI Mall.

closing: A low-density, design-led home by the lake at a fair price for own stay, especially for families with young children who will be ready for the new school next door.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this September 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. YTL Land's team gave Sean a private tour of the sales gallery, model and show unit; prices and the reclamation details are as he was told, so buyers should confirm them. Sean has lived in Puchong.
